West Side Original Maxwell Street Closed Days After Fatal Shooting, Failed Building Inspection

The Original Maxwell Street location in West Garfield Park failed a business inspection Friday, days after a 30-year-old mother was killed outside the restaurant.
by Charles Thrush 15 hours agoAugust 23, 2026

WEST GARFIELD PARK — A popular West Side hot dog stand has closed days after failing a building inspection and less than a week after a woman was shot and killed outside of the restaurant.

Original Maxwell Street, 3801 W. Harrison Ave., was closed to the public Sunday, though it is not clear if the closure was voluntary or forced by the city.

A worker was seen pasting handwritten signs onto a few barrels placed around the perimeter of the business, with the signs directing customers to the Original Maxwell Street near Cicero Avenue and Jackson Boulevard. The worker declined comment.

The closure came after the business failed a building inspection Friday.

A video posted to Instagram by the outlet ChicagoMediaTakeout shows an “off limits” sign posted by the city’s Department of Buildings, with the date of the building closure order listed as Friday. In the video, the building closure order that was posted to the restaurant was obscured by what appeared to be poster board taped over the notice.

The city’s closure order notice was not visible on the restaurant Sunday.

The building inspection, which was spurred by a complaint, found eight code violations, including for having “extreme flying insects,” “extreme unsanitary” conditions caused by animals, structural issues and missing smoke/carbon monoxide detectors, according to a city database.

It is unclear if the building issues were resolved by Sunday. Building inspection records do not show the property has passed a re-inspection since Friday. Spokespeople for the city’s buildings department and Original Maxwell Street did not return requests for comment from Block Club on Sunday.

Covering up or removing a city notice is in direct violation of the city’s municipal code, which states that “no person shall remove any such notice or sign unless and until the business reopens.”

The fatal shooting occurred around 3:30 a.m. Aug. 16, when a 30-year-old woman was arguing with a man in the parking lot of the restaurant. The man pulled out his gun and shot her several times before he drove off in a silver SUV, police said.

First responders arrived and took the woman — identified as Yolanda Chaytor — to Stroger Hospital, where she was pronounced dead with multiple gunshot wounds throughout her head and body, police said.

Chaytor’s death leaves three small children without their mother and in need of “immediate care and support,” her sister, Sayisha Lloyd, wrote in a GoFundMe.

Lloyd told ABC7 that Chaytor was an artist who worked two jobs to care for her children, ages 5, 7, and 8, and that she visited Maxwell Street to get some late-night food after visiting a friend in the area.

The family is seeking funds to help lay Chaytor to rest and help her children move forward. The GoFundMe has raised nearly $3,000 towards a $4,500 goal as of Sunday.

“This loss has shaken our family to the core, and I never imagined we would be facing something like this while trying to hold each other together,” Chaytor wrote on the GoFundMe page.

Area detectives are investigating the shooting.
